dedicated_requirements: Throughput: sustain 350-450 RPS on transaction scoring endpoints during normal peak; burst to 800 RPS for short windows (blackout protection).
Latency SLO: p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms for 32-64 token responses; critical auth path requires p95 < 200ms absolute or failover to sync-cache.
Reserved GPU planning: baseline 8x H100-class GPUs (reserved), autoscale headroom +4 GPUs per region; want clear burst billing model and warm-standby pricing.
SLA: target 99.95% uptime for dedicated pool; credits for >0.05% downtime; include MAINT windows (max 6 hours/quarter) and advance notice protocols.
Capacity planning: require explicit tail-latency reports and token/sec throughput profiles by model and seq-len distribution before signature.
Routing & failover: cross-region failover (us-east-1 -> us-west-2) with automated health checks + traffic shifting; minimal RTO target 3 minutes for full failover.
Fallback design: model-variant fallback (primary full-precision 13B -> quantized 6B 8-bit) for degraded quality but maintained latency; per-route fallback policies configurable in console.
Graceful degradation: prefer queueing + shedding non-critical routes, reducing max_token, disabling streaming to maintain SLOs on critical endpoints.
Observability: token-level cost & latency breakdown, per-request traces, and audit-able rollout logs required for compliance.
Security & residency: private VPC endpoint, customer KMS integration, audit logs retained 1 year for payments compliance.
Acceptance testing: run three full stress cycles (gradual ramp, sustained plateau, sudden spike) with reproducible traffic generator; success criteria defined in SOW.
Operational readiness: runbook for failover, rollback, capacity alerts (cpu/gpu/mem/kv-cache hit-rate), and support escalation path (SE on-call + CSM).
negotiation_notes: Legal: asking for liability cap adjustments and explicit credit tiers for downtime > 0.05%.
